extracted.intended_audience: federal contracting officers, DOD/Navy acquisition and procurement officials, agency policy implementers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for implementing OMB Circular A-76 (cost-comparison between in-house and private-sector performance) and the DOD/Navy Commercial-Industrial Activities (CITA) program. Focuses on when to contract-out, required documentation, cost-comparison methods, thresholds, review/approval procedures, and related procurement safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary reliance on private sector
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government should primarily rely on the private sector when acquiring property and services for Government use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes objective of effective and efficient accomplishment of Government programs rather than benefit to a particular segment of the economy; reflected in policy history and legislative proposals (e.g., proposed S-5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherently Governmental functions performed in-house
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain functions are inherently Governmental and must be performed in-house with Government personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include discretionary application of Government authority, monitoring transactions and entitlements, and maintenance of in-house core capabilities in research and development. Such functions are excluded from contracting-out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pursue most economical performance via rigorous cost comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: When commercial performance is feasible and no overriding factors require in-house performance, the most economical performance should be pursued including a rigorous and thorough comparison of in-house versus contractor costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cost-comparison process is the cornerstone of CITA support service contracting; agencies must follow common rules and use the Cost Comparison Handbook to produce consistency, predictability, and equity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of personal services contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal services contracts that create an employer-employee relationship between the Government and a contractor are prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Circular A-76 explicitly prohibits use of the Circular to justify personal services contracting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cannot convert solely due to personnel ceilings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular will not be used to justify conversion solely on the basis of personnel ceiling restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversions must be justified on substantive grounds (cost, availability, national defense, etc.), not to evade staffing limits or ceilings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use Circular inconsistent with laws/treaties
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular shall not be used when it is inconsistent with any laws, treaties, or international agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal constraints take precedence over Circular policy; agencies must ensure compliance with applicable legal obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for excess property/services from other agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Excess property and services available from other agencies should be used in preference to new starts or conversions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should consider interagency reuse (e.g., GSA programs) before initiating new in-house capabilities or contracting conversions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three exceptions to reliance on private sector
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised Circular combines prior five exceptions into three: (1) no satisfactory commercial source available (including delay/disruption), (2) in interest of National Defense to maintain Government capacity, (3) Government can perform at a lower cost than private sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the only permitted bases for retaining or providing work in-house absent commercial reliance; each exception has specific documentation and approval expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification for nonavailability requires extensive documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Justifying in-house performance due to nonavailability of commercial sources requires extensive documentation of attempts to locate or develop an adequate commercial source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At a minimum, announcements must be made in the Commerce Business Daily and assistance sought from GSA, SBA, and similar organizations. Strikes, urgency, or classification alone are insufficient justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: National defense justification criteria and approval level
rubrics_metrics.description: National defense justification for an in-house CITA must relate to training/career development/rotation of military personnel, direct combat support, or maintaining core capability in intermediate/depot level maintenance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such justifications must be approved at the Military Department Assistant Secretary level (e.g., ASN (MRA&L) for the Navy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Common ground rules for cost comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular establishes common ground rules for equitable cost comparisons between in-house and contract costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key rules include: (1) use the same scope of work and level of performance for both analyses; (2) use the standard cost factors specified in the Cost Comparison Handbook; (3) use full costing in the Government estimate; (4) recommend pre-priced options to preclude 'buy-ins' and amortize contractor startup costs; (5) obtain contract price by soliciting firm bids or proposals with the full intent to award if more cost-effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory use of Cost Comparison Handbook (Supplement No. 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a cost comparison is to be prepared, agencies must use Supplement No. 1 (the Cost Comparison Handbook).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook provides detailed guidance necessary to compare in-house and contract costs on an equitable basis and is intended to produce uniformity and reduce disputes about methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dollar threshold for required cost comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular raises the dollar limit for which a cost comparison is required from $50,000 to $100,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No in-house activity valued in excess of $100,000 will be converted to contract performance unless justified by a cost study; this threshold guides when formal cost comparisons are mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion/new-start differential thresholds (10% / 10%+25%)
rubrics_metrics.description: An existing in-house activity will not be converted to contract performance unless conversion results in savings of more than 10% of estimated Government personnel costs. A new start will be contracted-out unless potential savings by Government in-house performance are greater than 10% of Government personnel costs plus 25% of equipment and facilities costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These differentials are designed to maintain the status quo for existing in-house work while favoring contracting-out for new programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement and protections for set-aside programs
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular encourages use of set-aside programs to ensure small businesses (including disadvantaged) receive a fair portion of Government contracts and protects prior set-aside awards from re-review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracts previously awarded under set-aside programs will not be reviewed again for possible in-house performance. New requirements suitable for set-aside should be offered for contract without a cost comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventory compilation and review-schedule requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must compile a complete inventory of all CITAs, update it annually, establish an initial three-year review schedule published for public review, and for activities retained in-house schedule follow-on reviews at least once every five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Greater detail in reporting is required under the revised guidelines and review schedules must be made public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative review procedures for in-house/contract decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must establish procedures to resolve questions on in-house/contract decisions; upon written request an affected party is entitled to review by an official of the same or higher level than the initial decision-maker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reviewing official must assure fairness and compliance with policy; the decisions of the reviewing official are final and not subject to arbitration, negotiation, or other agreements with the affected party. This review applies only to the decision to contract-out or perform in-house, not award selection among contractors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain contract price via firm bids/proposals with intent to award
rubrics_metrics.description: Contract price used in comparisons must be obtained by soliciting firm bids or proposals from the private sector with the full intent to award a contract if it is more cost-effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The firm bid/offer procedure should be used to ensure realistic contractor pricing and prevent speculative or non-binding offers; Navy directives (NAVSUPINST, NAVMAT PPM) provide guidance to contracting officers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use pre-priced options to preclude buy-ins and amortize startup costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Use pre-priced options to the maximum extent possible to preclude 'buy-ins' and allow for amortization of contractor startup costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-priced options reduce incentive for contractors to underbid initial work (buy-in) and allow fair allocation of startup investments over contract options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of standard cost factors and full costing for Government estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government estimate must use standard cost factors (as specified in the Handbook) and full costing in preparing the Government estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Earlier Transmittal Memorandums used incremental costing; the revised Circular standardizes on full costing and specific cost factors because labor/benefit rates (insurance/retirement) significantly affect cost-comparison outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification and reporting requirements to Congress (DOD)
rubrics_metrics.description: DOD must certify to Congress that in-house cost calculations for functions under review are based on the most efficient and cost-effective organization for in-house performance and must meet reporting requirements to keep Congress informed of implementation progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory reporting and certification help ensure oversight and that A-76 is not used to circumvent civilian personnel ceilings or other statutory constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: EEO impact assessment and CNO approval for Navy actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Navy activities must provide an assessment of the Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) impact of a contract award decision; no contracts nor RIF notices will be issued until specific CNO approval is received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This adds an employment-equity and high-level concurrence step to Navy implementation beyond cost comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Firm bid/offer procedure responsibilities for contracting officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting officers must follow firm bid/offer procedures and associated responsibilities when supporting the CITA program and cost-comparison process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NAVSUPINST and CNM procurement memoranda provide definitive guidance on the contracting officer's role in implementing firm bid/offer procedures in support of CITA solicitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public review and comment on proposed revisions and interim guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed revisions to implementing directives and interim guidance are to be published for public review with comment periods (e.g., Federal Register or public notices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OFPP and OMB historically published proposed revisions for public review and comment; interim messages and letters were used during revision processes.
